chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj and Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The mother and the daughter are equal, when he does not enter with her, meaning when he marries the woman then divorces her before entering with her, then if he wishes he may marry her mother, and if he wishes he may marry her daughter.

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: consummated the marriage / entered with her

ai.seo_question: Can a man marry the mother or daughter of a woman he divorced before consummation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific condition of 'dakhul' (consummation) as the threshold for establishing the permanent prohibition of 'mu'akkadah' (definite kinship) between a woman and her mother or daughter. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling distinguishes between mere contractual marriage and the actualization of marital rights, allowing a man to marry either the mother or the daughter if he divorces the first wife before consummation. This principle underscores the importance of physical union in solidifying the mahram relationship in Islamic law.
